newsitem.title: PERU: Peru still negotiates banks' Brady options - sources.
newsitem.headline: Peru still negotiates banks' Brady options - sources.

text.p: The Peruvian government is still negotiating with creditor banks to finalize bond selections under the Brady Plan to restructure the bulk of the nation's foreign commercial debt, Economy Ministry sources said Tuesday.
"They are still negotiating. It's not clear when they are going to finalize this," one of the sources said. "We expect President (Alberto) Fujimori to make the announcement once it is complete."
Peru had announced a July 31 deadline for banks to choose their bond options and an August 9 date for the government to accept these formally.
However, the negotiations have dragged on in recent weeks without an official explanation for the delay.

Peru reached a preliminary Brady agreement with its bank creditors last October which, according to the government, would lead to an approximately $5 billion reduction on the total $10.56 billion owed.

Market sources, however, put the Brady deal debt at around $8.4 billion -- $4.2 billion principal, plus $4.2 billion in past due interest. These sources estimate a 40-50 percent reduction, depending on how much debt Peru decides to buy back. Economy Minister Jorge Camet said recently that the majority of the 400 creditor banks were tending towards the FLIRB bonds under the options offered in the Brady plan.

Camet said Monday that 18 percent of Peru's proposed 24.765 billion sol 1997 budget was earmarked for foreign debt payments. At the estimated average exchange rate for 1997 of 2.70 soles to the dollar, this would represent $1.651 billion.
